# Nika

> Nika turns repeatable AI work into a `.nika` workflow file you keep: checked before it runs, run with the model you choose, proven afterwards. One Rust binary (`nika`, AGPL-3.0-or-later) with a terminal Session and a command line, plus a TypeScript SDK (`@supernovae-st/nika` on npm) for applications; the language specification is Apache-2.0. A workflow has four verbs (`infer · exec · invoke · agent`) and a nine-key envelope (`nika` · `model` · `inputs` · `const` · `secrets` · `permits` · `run` · `tasks` · `outputs`, in any order); `nika: <kebab-id>` names every file. People describe work to bare `nika` (the Session), which proposes such a file for review, or write the file directly; either way it is checked before it runs, saving never runs it, and each run leaves a hash-chained trace. 0.124 is the current release line. Work stays focused on maintenance, security and the media capabilities workflows need; native video is planned for 0.125. There is no hosted service.

## Use Nika

- [Documentation index](https://docs.nika.sh/llms.txt): docs.nika.sh, indexed for agents. The documentation describes the released 0.124.1.
- [llms-install.md](llms-install.md): Installing the `nika` binary — the agent-lane runbook (package managers first, then a verified tarball · verify · prove offline · wire MCP · uninstall clean).
- [README.md#try-it-in-two-minutes](README.md#try-it-in-two-minutes): Install, describe a first workflow in the Session with no AI account, set up a provider key, then compile · check · run · verify a file directly. Ends with the current limits.
- [docs/usage/conversational-session.md](docs/usage/conversational-session.md): Bare `nika` on a terminal — describe · clarify · review · save (`yes`) · run (`run it`) · inspect (`/proof`). Provider keys come from the environment (DeepSeek example); the AI choice is kept in `~/.nika/session-intelligence.json`. Covers intelligence selection, `/restore`, knowledge provenance, the optional Jev decision model and downgrade limits.
- [TypeScript SDK quick start](https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/start/quickstart): run, stream and verify workflows from an application with `@supernovae-st/nika`, which bundles the engine of its own version.
- [Known limits in 0.124](https://docs.nika.sh/changelog/known-limits): what this release does not do, in plain words, each with a way around it.
- [docs/ops/README.md](docs/ops/README.md): `nika serve` — the resident schedule firer and the authenticated HTTP door, with its systemd unit and TLS proxy. [docs/ops/mcp-servers.md](docs/ops/mcp-servers.md): MCP servers a workflow invokes (declare · approve · confinement).
- [docs/qa/delivery-a-2026-09.md](docs/qa/delivery-a-2026-09.md): A historical qualification of the conversational path on 0.120.3: six synthetic journeys, one macOS installation, not a general reliability claim.
- [docs/architecture/session-history.md](docs/architecture/session-history.md): Where Session history lives, how reopening and recovery work, and their limits.

## Contribute

This repository is the "Diamond" rebuild: a layered Rust workspace (L0 primitives → L5 binary) where every crate passes a 12-gate admission protocol. Read these before changing the engine.

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): The cross-tool agent operating manual for contributors (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Codex). Hard rules, the 12-gate admission, tooling to run.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): What is in scope for the 0.124 line (security fixes, bug fixes, compatibility, documentation), the admission flow and the DCO sign-off.
- [DIAMOND.md](DIAMOND.md): The Diamond rewrite philosophy — why an orphan-branch rebuild, CRAFT-not-extraction.
- [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md): Where the 0.124 line stands (maintenance, security and the media capabilities workflows need; native video is planned for 0.125), then how the engine was built; the historical plan's forward items are not commitments. Run `bash scripts/refresh-status.sh` for the live canonical state (no volatile counts are hardcoded in docs).

## Architecture (the non-negotiables)

- [docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE-0.123.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE-0.123.md): The cooperative intent direction 0.123 converged toward, amended 6 October 2026. Target responsibilities, evidence, repair and migration acceptance; not a claim that the released runtime implements or qualifies all of them.
- [docs/architecture/forward-compat-invariants.md](docs/architecture/forward-compat-invariants.md): 8 patterns + 10 rules. Gate 12. Public API is protected; only strictly-additive changes pass.
- [docs/architecture/crate-layer-registry.md](docs/architecture/crate-layer-registry.md): L0→L4 layer discipline, allowed I/O axes, strict downward dependencies.
- [docs/architecture/BLUEPRINT_2036.md](docs/architecture/BLUEPRINT_2036.md): Historical direction, never ratified (a proposal): the crate ladder (cap 100), the collapse-vs-publish principle and the long horizon it once described. Not planned work.
- [docs/architecture/VISION_2040_intelligence-layer.md](docs/architecture/VISION_2040_intelligence-layer.md): Historical, non-binding direction — the intelligence layer it imagined (LSP, the workflow generator, agent-comprehension, memory, Nika-OS). Not planned work.

## How to work in this repo

- [.claude/rules/diamond-discipline.md](.claude/rules/diamond-discipline.md): The hard rules — read-only `brouillon`, 0 unwrap/expect in `src/`, ≤2,500 LOC/file, `#[non_exhaustive]` error enums, every I/O behind a kernel trait.
- [.claude/rules/commit-granularity.md](.claude/rules/commit-granularity.md): Atomic commits, the mandatory admission commit-body format, `Co-Authored-By: Nika 🦋` (never "Claude").
- [docs/adr/adr-003-12-gate-admission.md](docs/adr/adr-003-12-gate-admission.md): The 12-gate crate admission protocol.
- [docs/adr/adr-090-structural-doctrine-enforcement.md](docs/adr/adr-090-structural-doctrine-enforcement.md): The enforcement discipline — gates project a single source of truth.

## Gates (mechanical enforcement)

- [scripts/hygiene/README.md](scripts/hygiene/README.md): The hygiene vector catalog (`bash scripts/hygiene/check-all.sh`). Supply-chain (cargo-deny), ADR-081 computer-use guards, error one-voice, public-API coverage, and more.
- [scripts/ci/check-mutation-floor.sh](scripts/ci/check-mutation-floor.sh): The real Gate 5 — `cargo-mutants` kill-floor enforcement (admission/CI tier).

## Optional (depth on demand)

- [docs/crate-specs/](docs/crate-specs/): One spec per crate (purpose, public API, layer, gate status). The Gate-1 artifact.
- [docs/adr/](docs/adr/): The Architecture Decision Records — every locked decision, with bidirectional reference graph (validated by `scripts/adr/validate.sh`).
- [docs/architecture/](docs/architecture/): The full architecture corpus.
